title: Apricot Tarte Tatin with Crisp Pastry
changes_from_base: Apricot halves in place of apples, an egg-free crisp pastry, and the fruit is cooled and the tart chilled before a hot, fast bake.
summary: Classic Tatin made with apricot halves and a crisp, egg-free pastry, chilled first and then baked hot and fast.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: add the last bit only if needed

steps.title: Rub in
steps.text: process the flour, sugar, salt and butter for about 5 s, until like coarse crumbs. Add the water and pulse briefly until it looks like small peas, not a ball.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.text: tip it out, knead lightly until it holds, pat into a 15 cm disc, wrap and chill at least 20 min.

steps.title: Apricots
steps.text: melt the butter and sugar in the pan, then arrange the apricot halves in rings, cut side up. Cook over moderate heat until the sugar turns a golden caramel, watching so it does not burn. Leave to cool completely. Cooling the fruit stops the caramel melting the butter in the pastry.

steps.title: Lid
steps.text: roll the pastry to a 25 cm round, lay it over the cold fruit, trim the excess and tuck the edge down. Chill 30 min.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Prick the pastry all over with the knife tip and bake 20-25 min, until crisp and golden. Pricking lets steam escape so the pastry stays flat and crisp.

steps.title: Turn out
steps.text: leave 5 min, then flip onto the plate. If any apricots stick, lift them off and put them back in place.

tips: Do not overwork the dough; small lumps of butter make it flaky.
Apricots that are ripe but firm keep their shape best.
Use a cast-iron pan if you have one, as it holds heat evenly.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best on the day. Cover and keep in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat in a 160 °C oven for 10 min.
